approach: Reuse the committed round-3 job-plan and critique records as the kept plan and findings. Add one optional field, `resumed_from: Option<JobId>`, to JobPlan (serde default, skipped when none). reading.rs gets `planning_resume_seed`, which qualifies only a cap-stopped predecessor. run.rs seeds round 1 of the retry's planning loop with it, so round 1 is the revision round and the first critic round sees the revised plan. status.rs computes planning rounds and cost per landed job over the retry chain, split at the first resumed plan. display.rs prints it. All new tests go in listed files (lifecycle.rs, reading.rs, status.rs, display.rs, records.rs, briefs.rs). docs/records.md is not touched. The only files outside the list are two test-fixture literals that the compiler forces, named below.

decisions.choice: Keep the existing job-plan and critique records as the kept plan and findings. Add only the optional `resumed_from` on JobPlan.
decisions.reason: The closing already commits the round-3 plan and critique. The marker lets status split before and after from records alone.

rejected.why: It duplicates stored data and is a bigger schema change.

rejected.option: Infer 'resumed' from the retry's outcome text
rejected.why: Earlier retries of cap stops planned fresh, so the split would be wrong.

decisions.choice: Seed round 1 of the retry's own loop with the kept revision, then run the normal loop under the same cap.
decisions.reason: This gives exactly one revision round before the critic. Cap and grading are unchanged.

rejected.option: Send the kept plan straight to the critic
rejected.why: The findings would go unaddressed and be repeated.

decisions.choice: Qualify by structure plus a shared `PLANNING_CAP_REASON` const matched with `contains`. A unit test uses an outcome string copied verbatim from a pre-change cap stop (for example 20261026-145955-s7e2).
decisions.reason: Old records hold only the literal text, round, summary and findings. The shared const keeps the stop and the check together.

rejected.why: The request covers only the cap stop.

rejected.option: A typed stop reason in the outcome record
rejected.why: Larger schema change, and old jobs would not carry it.

decisions.choice: Status reports chain totals: for each planned landed job, follow `retried_job` back through every predecessor (visited-set guard), adding plan counts and planner and critic invocation cost. Each chain is counted once, at its landed job. The landed job's own figures are shown beside the totals.
decisions.reason: The wasted spend sits on the failed predecessor. A per-job measure would miss the saving.

rejected.option: Count only the landed job's own rounds and cost
rejected.why: Before and after would not show the saving.

decisions.choice: Cutover is the dispatch time of the first job whose plan has `resumed_from`. A landed chain is 'after' if its landed job was dispatched at or after it. Print the cutover job id and time, and label 'after' as 'since the first resumed planning'.
decisions.reason: It comes from records alone, with no clock or version heuristic. The label prevents reading it as 'since shipped'.

rejected.option: Compare resumed jobs only against non-resumed ones
rejected.why: That is not before and after, and resumed landed jobs are few.

decisions.choice: Put integration tests in crates/athena-cli/tests/lifecycle.rs, using Scenario from tests/common.
Do not edit docs/records.md (answers finding 2). The field is documented by its rustdoc comment in records.rs and by the CHANGELOG entry.
decisions.reason: The file is outside the listed deliverables.

decisions.choice: Add `resumed_from: None` to the test JobPlan literals in store.rs `plan()` and admission.rs `findings_for_path` (answers findings 3 and 4). These two one-line edits are the only edits outside the list.
decisions.reason: JobPlan has no Default and no `..` base in these literals (read at admission.rs:488 and store.rs:467), so any new field on it fails to compile there. A marker elsewhere would need a typed, checkable home, and the Job and Outcome records would need the same fixture edits. The edits are mechanical, change no behavior, and add no new tests.

rejected.option: Hide the field in an existing text field
Derive the split without a marker
rejected.why: Pre-change retries of cap stops are indistinguishable from resumed ones.

risks.risk: The new JobPlan field breaks struct literals in test modules or a schema or gate check.
risks.mitigation: The field is optional and skipped when none, so old records parse. Fix literals as the compiler reports them and run the full suite.

risks.risk: A retry resumes after the base or config changed, or the old plan names files that no longer exist.
risks.mitigation: The reading allows it. Athena's existing plan checks still run on the revised plan and send it back if wrong.

risks.risk: Round 1 of a resumed job is a revision, which changes what `FirstRoundCounts` means for it.
risks.mitigation: Leave `FirstRoundCounts` as is and note it in the CHANGELOG.

risks.risk: A small 'after' group makes the mean misleading, and 'after' may be misread as 'since shipped'.
risks.mitigation: Print job counts, the cutover job and time, and the 'since the first resumed planning' label.

risks.risk: The cap-stop wording changes and the reason match breaks.
risks.mitigation: A shared const used by the stop and the check, a verbatim old-outcome unit test, and an end-to-end stop-then-resume test.

risks.risk: Chain walking double-counts a predecessor, or loops on bad records.
risks.mitigation: Count each chain once at its landed job, guard the walk with a visited set, and test a three-job chain.

demonstrations.method: Integration test in lifecycle.rs. A Scenario's critic returns Revise in all three rounds, so `go` stops at the cap. Then `athena.retry` and `go` run on the new job, with the script wrapped to record each spec's role and prompt.
demonstrations.observes: The first retry planner prompt contains the kept round-3 approach and every round-3 finding. After the retry's reader the calls are exactly Planner then Critic. The first retry critic prompt contains the revised approach and not the kept one. The retry's job-plan-1.json has `resumed_from` equal to the old job.
demonstrations.fails_without: Without the seed the retry's first planner prompt is a fresh brief with no kept approach or findings, so the contains assertions fail. The call order and the critic's prompt would also differ.

demonstrations.method: Integration tests in lifecycle.rs retry a job that stopped on a plan reject, one that stopped on a producer timeout (`deadline_script`), and one that failed verification. A reading.rs unit test checks `planning_resume_seed` is None for these and for a non-retry request.
demonstrations.observes: Each retry's first planner prompt has no revision section, no kept-plan text and no findings. Its job-plan-1.json has no `resumed_from`.
demonstrations.fails_without: If resume applied to every retry or to any planning stop, the reject case would show the kept plan in the prompt and the absence assertions would fail.

demonstrations.method: status.rs unit tests with hand-built Records. Before group: a cap-stopped predecessor plus a landed retry that planned fresh. After group: a cap-stopped predecessor plus a landed retry whose round-1 plan has `resumed_from`. An unlanded job and an unplanned landed job must be excluded. A display.rs render test checks the printed text. A third test checks the 'after' group is empty when no plan is resumed.
demonstrations.observes: Chain-total mean rounds and mean USD match the fixture, with predecessors included, and the own figures sit beside them. Group counts and the cutover job id and time are right. The text shows both groups and the label 'since the first resumed planning'.
demonstrations.fails_without: With no planning-cost computation there are no such lines and the numeric assertions fail. A per-job-only computation fails the predecessor-included totals.

demonstrations.method: The same lifecycle test loads the retry's committed records. The kept plan and findings are the old job's job-plan-3 and critique-3. The retry's job-plan-1 carries only a job id in `resumed_from`. A records.rs round-trip test checks that old records without the field still parse.
demonstrations.observes: Records load and `athena.check_history()` reports no violations. `resumed_from` holds only a job id. Fixture text has no secrets or personal data.
demonstrations.fails_without: Without the marker the `resumed_from` assertion fails. Without the optional-field default, the old-record round-trip test in records.rs fails.

demonstrations.method: Run the three Athena checks as one command chain.
demonstrations.command: cargo fmt --all --check && cargo clippy --all-targets --locked -- -D warnings && cargo test --locked
demonstrations.fails_without: The new tests (resume, fresh retry, planning_cost, render, round-trip) are part of the suite. If the behavior or its tests were missing, or the field edits left store.rs or admission.rs not compiling, clippy or test would exit non-zero. Unformatted code fails fmt.

demonstrations.method: Read the Unreleased section of the diff.
demonstrations.observes: A new entry describes the resumable planning stop (kept plan and findings; retry runs one revision round then the critic). It also describes planning rounds and cost per landed job in status as chain totals, with 'after' meaning 'since the first resumed planning'.

open_questions: Whether Scenario in tests/common/mod.rs can record prompts and call order as the tests need; if not, wrap the script in the test itself.
A job dispatched with no recorded time counts as 'before' (assumption).
If the reading's deliverable list is strict, the two fixture edits in store.rs and admission.rs need explicit approval; no typed alternative compiles without them.
